preconditions.description: The number of vertices in the broom is between 2 and 300,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u < v <= n for u, v, _ in edges) and len(edges) == n - 1
preconditions.description: The broom is a valid tree with n vertices, where edges are directed from parent to child (u to v), and there are exactly n-1 edges.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, str) and len(x) == 1 and x.islower() for _, _, x in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge is labeled with a single lowercase Latin letter.
Vertex 1 is the root of the broom.

postconditions.expression: min_size == min(broom_size(p) for p in range(1, max_word_length + 1) if p <= max_word_length) and min_size >= 1
postconditions.description: The minimum possible size of the broom after simplification is the smallest size achievable by choosing any valid p (1 ≤ p ≤ max_word_length), where max_word_length is the length of the longest word in the language.

postconditions.expression: chosen_p == min(p for p in range(1, max_word_length + 1) if broom_size(p) == min_size)
postconditions.description: The chosen p is the smallest integer that achieves the minimum broom size, or any valid p if multiple exist.
The chosen p must result in the minimum possible broom size.
